prose_changes.old: The mainline denominations were alive in 2010; what closed around 1990 was this particular century of theirs. Their membership peaked in the mid-1960s and turned down after that, and from around 1990 the current that carried their questions went under the progressive label, which this map treats as their continuation. Their institutional legacy is large: the National Council of Churches from 1950, the World Council of Churches in Geneva, and a network of seminaries that trained the denominations' clergy and produced much of the century's biblical and theological scholarship. Barth's line ran into the Confessing Church, whose Barmen Declaration he drafted. And the argument with fundamentalism, fought out in dated documents on both sides, is the one this map draws as a standing tension rather than a settled question.
prose_changes.new: The mainline churches were alive in 2010. What closed around 1990 was this one century of theirs. Their numbers peaked in the mid-1960s and fell after that. From around 1990 the people who carried their questions often called their faith progressive. They left large bodies behind: the National Council of Churches from 1950, a home in the World Council of Churches, and many seminaries. Those seminaries trained the clergy and wrote much of the century's Bible scholarship. Barth's line ran into the Confessing Church, whose Barmen Declaration he drafted. And the argument with fundamentalism, fought out in dated texts on both sides, was never settled.
prose_changes.reason: Two map-layout remarks ('which this map treats as their continuation'; 'the one this map draws as a standing tension') rewritten in plain words. The progressive tie is now the link drafted as 'gave rise to'. Long sentences split for reading level. Every fact kept.
